pyproject.toml.description: Evidence-governed Kuramoto-XY quantum-control and differentiable-computation workbench

readme_excerpts:
`scpn-quantum-control` is an evidence-governed workbench for turning
coupled-oscillator models into quantum-control experiments, simulator studies,
gradient-bearing optimisation loops, and auditable hardware-result packages.
It is for teams that need a repeatable path from a physical model to a result
that can be reviewed, reproduced, cited, or used in an application pilot.

If your team needs reproducible research or product-grade experimentation, the
repository provides:

It is positioned for use-cases where decision quality depends on evidence:
engineering teams that need a consistent pathway from model specification to
observable contracts, and research teams that need explicit failure modes rather
than implied coverage.

sections.heading: Purpose and boundaries
sections.excerpt:
This page documents the software architecture in a way that supports technical due
diligence and long-lived integration. The design objective is to keep
problem-to-experiment flow deterministic while allowing each subsystem to evolve
with clear contracts.

The architecture intentionally separates:

- **core transforms** (`bridge`, `phase`, `analysis`) from
- **execution substrates** (`hardware`, `benchmarks`) and
- **evidence/control surfaces** (`release`, `hardware status`, campaign artefacts).

The coupled-phase-oscillator (Kuramoto) acceleration substrate that formerly lived
under `accel/` now ships as the standalone `oscillatools` distribution;
`scpn_quantum_control.accel` remains a deprecation shim that re-exports it (see
`DEPRECATIONS.md`).

This split is why the same repository can support both reproducible research
workflows and integration-oriented development.

sections.heading: Shared canonical encoding
sections.excerpt:
`canonical_encoding` is a dependency-free contracts owner for typed JSON bytes
and schema-prefixed SHA-256 digests. Both HAL backend profile exporters and
Studio workspace readers depend on this lower layer. The original
`studio_workspace.canonical` functions retain their defining names and pickle
paths while delegating encoding and hashing to the shared codec.
No HAL producer imports Studio to bind metadata; encoding domains and byte
corpora retain their established semantics.

sections.heading: Native provider semantics ownership
sections.excerpt:
The original HAL and seven native adapter owners consume immutable request and
submission contracts from `hardware.provider_semantics`. Native Qiskit Runtime
PUB extraction lives in `hardware.provider_measurement`; photonic, analog and
annealing records live in `hardware.provider_modalities`. Dependency direction
runs from adapters into these contract/extraction leaves, with no Studio or
numerical-engine back-edge. SDKs retain binding, compilation and numerical
execution ownership. Legacy raw codecs remain separate from the optional
`provider_semantics.v1` companion.

The [native HAL guide](hardware_guide.md#native-workload-and-result-semantics)
describes source/target custody, shared parameters, explicit final readout and
native outputs. Adapter selectors, local software execution, transport fixtures
and physical-device evidence retain distinct provenance.

sections.heading: Scientific problem inputs and parameter schemas
sections.excerpt:
`KuramotoProblem` remains the original symmetric coupling/frequency owner.
Its existing constructors, compilers and raw metadata codec retain their
contracts. `ScientificDesign` supplies an immutable declaration;
`ScientificProblemParameters(problem, design)` validates that declaration
against the actual problem and produces a separate `scientific_problem.v1`
companion. The original `oscillatools` numerical kernels remain independent
of Studio and Atlas. The scientific companion adapter
consumes the existing workspace `ParameterSpec`, typed float64 payloads and
canonical codec instead of defining another workspace format or solver.

The companion identity includes the declared model and coupling convention,
logical/physical coordinates, explicit graph, units, initial/history state,
observable, design objective and trainable parameter names. Arrays own immutable
byte buffers; caller edits and mutations of exported dictionaries cannot rebind
an existing identity. Topology contains sorted unique undirected index pairs,
covers every nonzero coupling, and retains declared zero-weight edges.

| Declaration | Phase dynamics | Quantum XY spin model |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `phase_kuramoto` | `quantum_xy` |
| Coupling convention | `pairwise_sum` or `population_mean` | Original `pairwise_sum` |
| Initial state | `float64 (N,)` phase angles | Normalized `complex128 (2**N,)` amplitudes |
| State unit | `rad` | `1` |
| Observable | `phase_order_parameter`, nonnegative weights with positive total | `spin_z`, finite per-qubit weights |
| History | Optional strictly increasing times ending at zero; final state equals initial state | Phase history refused |
| Objective | Simulation, synchronisation target in `[0,1]`, observable maximisation | Simulation, observable maximisation, gate-c

sections.heading: Circuit transformations and measurement preservation
sections.excerpt:
`scpn_quantum_control.compiler.compile_circuit_to_mlir` accepts a bound native
Qiskit circuit or a bounded static OpenQASM 2 source. It lowers the unitary body
through the original native transpiler to `rx`, `ry`, `rz` and `cx`, then attaches
the original trailing measurement/barrier block at its original bit indices.
Optimising the unitary body separately preserves phase-sensitive semantics that
an optimisation conditioned on final measurement could otherwise discard.
The transpiler receives no assumption that input qubits are zero. Its virtual
output permutations are materialised through native permutation synthesis before
readout is attached, preserving both arbitrary input states and original bit indices.

`qualify_circuit_pass` also qualifies an existing transformation, including the
original global unitary folding output. Its immutable `CircuitPassRecord` stores
both instruction IRs, exact source text and digests, real statement spans, register
indices, logical-to-physical layouts, observable correspondence, the explicit
global-phase policy and the measured reference error. Source offsets count Python
Unicode characters; line and column are one-based. Generated rotation source uses
round-trip decimal parameters instead of approximate multiples of pi.

The native `qiskit.quantum_info.Operator` reference checks every input basis,
after normalising declared qubit layouts. Readout comparison includes partial,
permuted and multi-register measurements, explicit output classical-bit layouts,
and the final assignment to each classical bit. The maximum complex128 operator
entry error must be at most `1e-12`; callers can tighten this bound. With
`allow_global_phase=True`, one constant phase may relate the full operators.
With `False`, that phase difference is also refused.

sections.heading: Phase-model conventions and original numerical owners
sections.excerpt:
[`kuramoto_conventions.md`](kuramoto_conventions.md) records the model, solver,
observable, gradient and source-declared backend matrix. Each row identifies
the actual original declaration, units, sign, normalisation, topology,
history and noise assumptions. Finite networks, exact finite reductions,
continuum reductions and quantum XY amplitudes retain separate identities.
Source/declaration hashes bind the generated JSON inventory; a declared backend
or test path does not establish installed availability or execution evidence.
The source producer refuses incomplete dispatch declarations before generating
either artefact, and its check mode preserves saved files on disagreement.

`build_scientific_phase_system(problem, design, dt=..., model=..., scheme=...)`
validates the original `KuramotoProblem` and supplied `ScientificDesign`, then
binds them to the original instantaneous finite `KuramotoSystem`, using its
existing Euler or RK4 evolution. It imports no Studio schemas or companion;
workspace consumers pass `parameters.problem` and `parameters.design` explicitly.
Networked forces sum supplied pairwise coefficients; a population-mean declaration explicitly
projects them to `K_nm/N`. The finite mean-field path requires equal effective
off-diagonal coefficients and recovers the original scalar coupling, rather
than averaging a heterogeneous network. Positive coupling uses
`sin(theta[k] - theta[j])`. Phases remain in radians without wrapping or
automatic unit conversion.

The factory refuses supplied delay history, quantum amplitudes, unsupported
model/solver pairs, nonfinite steps and invalid mean-field projections.
Delayed, noisy, inertial, adaptive, multiplex, reduced and force-only rows
retain their separate original entry points. Trajectories contain phases;
a declar

sections.heading: Solver times and termination
sections.excerpt:
The original `KuramotoSystem.trajectory_with_times` pairs each accepted fixed-step
state with the clock that evolved it. Its legacy `trajectory` still returns the
phase array. Fixed-step calls validate inputs and intermediate vector fields,
then accept the whole call's state and time together; rejected evolution retains
the pre-call state. This remains the original Euler/RK4 owner and force dispatch.

`solve_kuramoto_ivp` delegates adaptive/stiff integration and event interpolation
to SciPy. Its result keeps original success/status diagnostics, adds event roots
and states, and distinguishes `completed`, `event` and `failed` termination.
Terminal events can precede the first requested sample; partial failed output and
event arrays remain observable. Plastic-coupling and delayed paths retain their
own existing RK4 equations; linear lag interpolation and history derivative jumps
have separate accuracy limits. See [solver outcomes](kuramoto_solver_outcomes.md)
and the runnable scientific factory example for the exact public contracts.

sections.heading: Chimera and multiscale control composition
sections.excerpt:
`scpn_quantum_control.chimera_control` separates the surface into six
responsibility modules plus a public facade: immutable hierarchy/target
contracts, exact finite two-population synthesis, nested observables, composed
analytic objectives and unapplied proposals, topology-ledger projection
reports, and deterministic evidence custody. The package imports the production
`oscillatools` Sakaguchi force and Shanahan diagnostics, the existing
`phase.synchronisation_objectives` cluster term, and
`topology_control.constraints`; it does not duplicate those owners.

The dependency direction is one-way:

```text
chimera_control.schema
        ↓
chimera_control.synthetic ──→ oscillatools Sakaguchi/chimera diagnostics
        ↓
chimera_control.observables
        ↓
chimera_control.objectives ─→ phase.synchronisation_objectives
chimera_control.topology ───→ topology_control.constraints
        ↓
chimera_control.evidence ───→ deterministic JSON/Markdown + notebook 50
```

No external execution, controller mutation, hardware, provider, QPU, or
biological-data dependency enters this package. See
[Chimera and Multiscale Synchronisation Control](chimera_multiscale_control.md).

sections.heading: DLA and topology-constrained control composition
sections.excerpt:
`scpn_quantum_control.dla_topology_control` separates the surface into six
responsibility modules plus a public facade. Parity projection delegates its
forward map to `analysis.dla_parity_theorem`; topology sensitivity calls the
production `TopologyConstraintLedger.project` and supplies local JVP/VJP rules
only for fixed supported active sets. The synthetic objective, projected-
gradient trace, immutable support schema, and deterministic evidence remain
separate owners.

```text
dla_topology_control.schema
        ↓
dla_topology_control.parity ─────→ analysis.dla_parity_theorem
        ↓
dla_topology_control.objectives
        ↓
dla_topology_control.optimizer

dla_topology_control.projection ─→ topology_control.constraints
        ↓
dla_topology_control.evidence ───→ existing projected SPSA + notebook 51
```

The topology path refuses derivatives at sign and clipping kinks, active
total-weight rescaling, positive connectivity thresholds, and discrete or
persistent-homology changes. See
[DLA and Topology-Constrained Differentiable Control](dla_topology_constrained_control.md).

sections.heading: Multimodal forecasting composition
sections.excerpt:
`scpn_quantum_control.forecasting` separates multimodal forecasting into seven cohesive
owners: immutable multimodal custody, deterministic synthetic generation,
missingness-aware point forecasting, partial-observation scoring, residual
interval calibration, external composition ports, and digest-bound reporting.
The existing real-data and neural-operator benchmark modules remain independent;
the bounded forecasting product does not relabel their datasets or claims.

The dependency direction is one-way. The generator uses the established exact
Kuramoto simulator; model fitting consumes immutable batches; calibration
consumes a frozen model plus a disjoint calibration split; reporting consumes
certificates without owning numerical algorithms. The bridge module converts
interval widths into existing `InformationGainCandidate` records and a
terminal forecast into an existing `ControllerProposal`. Neither the sensing
nor controller surface imports forecasting, so no control/sensing back-edge is introduced.

Complete known simulator couplings are retained for the physics-residual
certificate. Consequently the partial-observation surface scores a forecast; it
does not infer hidden states, graph edges, or parameters. All domain tags remain
simulation-only, hardware requests fail closed, and controller proposals remain
unapplied. See [Multimodal Forecasting Under Partial
Observation](multimodal_forecasting.md).

sections.heading: Quantum-classical co-design composition
sections.excerpt:
`scpn_quantum_control.codesign` is a thin composition layer, not a new physics
or realtime-control stack. Its dependency direction is one-way: immutable
contracts feed a local phase-objective evaluator, estimator and controller;
latency and safety policies decide whether the proposal is applied to the next
simulator state; replay serialises the complete decision. The package consumes
`RealtimeFeedbackPort`, `QaoaMpcPort`, and policy-gated co-simulation adapters,
plus active-sensing, identity, and geometry observer records. It does not import a partner
repository or move plant-model ownership into this codebase.

The evaluator reuses the existing synchronisation objective and exact analytic
gradient, attaches the existing governed capability explanation, and can
compose one explicit bounded open-system case. A `ClosedLoopExecutionPolicy` is
required, but hardware execution remains refused even when that policy carries
a ticket. Logical timestamps make replay deterministic; measured workstation
timings live only in a separately labelled `functional_non_isolated` evidence
artefact. See [Quantum-Classical Co-Design Loop](quantum_classical_codesign_loop.md).

sections.heading: ML convergence evidence composition
sections.excerpt:
`scpn_quantum_control.ml_examples` is a thin evidence layer over three existing
owners: `phase.qnn_training`, `phase.qgnn`, and `qsnn.training`. Immutable task,
certificate, framework-row, and suite contracts feed one-way family-specific
runners; `suite.py` composes those results; `evidence.py` validates and writes
the canonical digest-bound JSON/Markdown pair. No trainer imports the evidence
package, so the dependency direction remains acyclic.

Only the bounded QNN path has native JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow adapters. The
matrix executes installed adapters and records missing, inapplicable, and
unsupported routes explicitly. QGNN and QSNN do not gain synthetic framework
adapters through this layer. The package owns orchestration and evidence, not a
numerical hot path; the actual message passing, Phase-QNode evaluation, dense
quantum layer, and parameter-shift work remain with their established owners.
See [QNN, QGNN, and QSNN convergence examples](ml_convergence_examples.md).

sections.heading: Studio Program-AD replay trust chain
sections.excerpt:
The Studio Program-AD replay card is an end-to-end verification chain, not a JavaScript
reimplementation of automatic differentiation. The v2 committed unit at
`data/studio/program_ad_replay_rational_20260714.json` freezes a rational
effect-IR program, finite scalar inputs, the Rust engine's exact value and
gradient, and a SHA-256 digest over the packed bytes consumed by the browser
kernel. The Python emitter rejects duplicate-key or non-standard JSON, malformed
engine responses, non-finite numbers, oversized IR, and oversized input arity;
its check mode distinguishes drift from an unreadable or unverifiable artifact.

The browser accepts only the exact v2 schema, artifact identity, claim boundary,
parameter targets, and declared digest. It recomputes the input SHA-256 with Web
Crypto before invoking the standalone Rust WASM replay. Changing the frozen
program and the expected result together therefore remains `unverifiable`, not
`match`. A canonical input whose recomputed value or gradient differs remains a
`mismatch`. The Rust parser shares the Python limits of 1,048,576 UTF-8 IR bytes
and 4,096 scalar inputs and rejects non-finite bindings before the bounded replay.

The wire layout and canonical replay bytes are unchanged from v1; v2 adds the
cryptographic binding and strict metadata contract. The numerical Program-AD
algorithm, rational fixture, and expected `[19; 6, 2]` result are unchanged, so
no comparison benchmark artifact is invalidated. Focused native Rust tests, a
release WASM build, real-WASM browser/component tests, and exact Python plus
TypeScript owner coverage are the applicable cross-language evidence.

sections.heading: Executed whole-program differentiation routes
sections.excerpt:
The compiler facade distinguishes four execution contracts:

| Route | Public entry point | Executed boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python interpreter | `compile_whole_program_ad_trace_to_executable` | Captured Program AD replay and reverse adjoints. |
| Native LLVM | `compile_whole_program_ad_trace_to_native_llvm_jit` | Verified LLVM IR compiled by llvmlite MCJIT, then called through native function pointers. |
| Native Rust | `value_and_grad_program_ad_effect_ir_with_rust` | The installed PyO3 extension executes its admitted effect-IR subset. |
| Browser WASM | `instantiateProgramAd` in `studio-web/src/shared/browser/programAd.ts` | A compiled Rust WASM module executes the bounded replay ABI. |

`compile_whole_program_ad_trace_to_mlir` emits textual interchange. Emitting or
parsing that text does not establish machine-code execution. Missing LLVM is
an explicit native compilation error; missing Rust produces an unavailable
result; absent or invalid WASM bytes fail instantiation. These routes do not
silently qualify QIR, CUDA-Q, provider execution or physical hardware.

For example, the existing public LLVM factory can compile a finite polynomial:

```python
import numpy as np
from scpn_quantum_control.compiler import compile_whole_program_ad_trace_to_native_llvm_jit
from scpn_quantum_control.differentiable import Parameter


def polynomial(values):
    return values[0] * values[0] + 2.0 * values[1]


kernel = compile_whole_program_ad_trace_to_native_llvm_jit(
    polynomial,
    np.array([3.0, 5.0], dtype=np.float64),
    (Parameter("x"), Parameter("y")),
)
value, gradient = kernel.value_and_grad([-2.0, 1.0])  # 6.0, [-4.0, 2.0]
```

Parameter order is fixed at compilation. The Python factories accept finite
parameter vectors and normalise native buffers to contiguo

sections.heading: Module responsibility policy
sections.excerpt:
Module boundaries in this codebase are governed by **single responsibility, not line
count**. A file is split when it holds two or more *independent* responsibility clusters;
a file whose definitions form a single connected, mutually-coupled dependency cluster is
kept whole, because splitting it would introduce artificial seams or import cycles without
improving cohesion. Physical line count is non-gating telemetry: there is no LOC admission,
failure, split, or exception threshold.

The reviewed policy is machine-readable in `tools/module_size_policy.json`. Every row records
the file kind, disposition, single responsibility (or current mixed responsibilities), direct
dependency boundary, and the condition that re-opens review; its stored line count is historical
telemetry only. `tools/audit_module_size_policy.py` rejects missing reviewed files, malformed
decisions, and growth in the explicit refactor-debt ratchet. It deliberately does not discover,
reject, or force-split modules from their LOC. The local no-test preflight and CI run that
responsibility gate. The stricter command below remains red while any reviewed refactor is open:

```bash
python tools/audit_module_size_policy.py --strict
```

Responsibility review is structural. Reviewers use internal call graphs, public API ownership,
state lifecycles, dependency direction, and change cadence to distinguish one cohesive cluster
from independent groups joined by a shared helper. Those signals are evidence, not a universal
language-independent classifier, so CI does not invent a godfile verdict from a heuristic score.
It fails only on explicit mixed-responsibility/refactor decisions, invalid responsibility records,
or lost reviewed owners. The separate test-quality audit can reject precisely enumerated bucket
test nam

sections.heading: Classical-to-Quantum Mapping
sections.excerpt:
Each module maps a classical SCPN computation to its quantum analog:

These are declared encoding or modelling choices. The phase Kuramoto ODE and
quantum XY spin dynamics have different state spaces and observables; matching
coupling/frequency coefficients does not establish dynamical equivalence.
Scientific problem companions keep the two models distinct.

| Classical (SCPN) | Quantum (this repo) | Mapping |
|-------------------|---------------------|---------|
| Stochastic LIF membrane potential | Ry(theta) rotation angle | theta = pi * (v - v_rest) / (v_threshold - v_rest) |
| Bitstream AND-gate synapse | CRy(theta_w) controlled rotation | P(out) = P(pre) * sin^2(theta_w/2) |
| STDP correlation learning | Parameter-shift gradient rule | dw = lr * pre * d<Z>/d(theta) |
| Kuramoto ODE (dtheta/dt) | XY Hamiltonian Trotter evolution | H = -K_ij(XX + YY) - omega_i Z_i |
| 16-layer UPDE coupling | 16-qubit spin chain | Knm -> J_ij entangling gates |
| MPC quadratic cost | QAOA Ising Hamiltonian | ||state - target||^2 -> ZZ + Z terms |
| Grad-Shafranov PDE | VQLS linear system | Laplacian A, source b -> A|x> ~ |b> |
| SPN token probability | Qubit amplitude | p -> amplitude encoding |
| Disruption feature vector | Amplitude-encoded state | 11-D -> 16-D zero-padded |

A differentiable, control-oriented toolkit for coupled-phase-oscillator (Kuramoto)
dynamics. It provides the model family, integrators, exact mean-field reductions,
stability and continuation analysis, differentiation, and control primitives as a
light, standalone distribution whose only hard dependencies are **NumPy** and
**SciPy**. Every acceleration or interoperability tier (a Rust engine, Julia, JAX,
PyTorch, matplotlib, scikit-learn) is an optional extra; the pure-Python NumPy
floor always runs.

`oscillatools` is extracted from
[`scpn-quantum-control`](https://github.com/anulum/scpn-quantum-control), where the
toolkit originated, so that the coupled-oscillator surface can be installed without
that project's quantum-provider dependency stack.
A generated capability handbook and manifest enumerate the full public surface.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.excerpt:
QPU-RESULT-PACK is an offline evidence boundary between completed-result producers, an explicitly installed numerical programme, a shared evidence runtime and document consumers.

Original bytes and acquisition facts remain separate from normalised views. Counts, requested shots, observed totals, timestamps, calibration association and reported quantities have distinct meanings. Numerical agreement, provider assurance, producer authenticity, measurement qualification and current eligibility are separate outcomes.

The intended public workflow consists of capture, import, derive, seal, verify, inspect and render. Inspection and rendering preserve data without executing a received programme. A caller-owned installed binding controls execution; artefact fields cannot select code. Verification produces a new observation rather than mutating the original pack.

This checkout currently contains repository documents and metadata. Its domain implementation is not yet integrated or accepted. [The detailed boundary](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [threat model](docs/THREAT_MODEL.md) describe the contracts that implementation must preserve.

sections.heading: Evidence and numerical boundary
sections.excerpt:
A completed-job producer supplies original observations and separate custody facts. Import preserves foreign bytes, original representations and field origin. A count total, requested resource, calibration label and observed timestamp are distinct assertions.

Derivation binds the actual installed programme, environment lock, ordered inputs, output schema, full scalar inventory, precision, units, comparison and optional seed. Earlier raw output is validated before later execution/output wrappers. Failure, cancellation and resource refusal retain actual diagnostics without producing a successful output.

The shared runtime owns content addressing, canonicalisation, signing and Common evaluation. The pack owns domain comparison and policy conjunction. Common success does not certify physical measurement or current domain eligibility. Verification creates a separate immutable report for the explicit policy and time.

Caller-owned unsigned and protected trust contexts have different fields. Selected source versions and installed types must agree with the whole request and evaluation inputs. Historical intervals need genuine event sources; an operational evaluation witness is not their replacement.

Inspection retains complete claims, reasons, quantities, references and unavailable states without executing programmes or granting eligibility. Rendering escapes foreign text and preserves full scope. Assurance resolves actual class information rather than relabelling a declared validation token.

The standalone domain implementation is not yet integrated. These are required public semantics, not observed whole-workflow acceptance.

retained reference uses original raw JSON bytes and an omitted schema label.
`evaluation_documents` now selects the fixed original Common-report grammar
independently while preserving that raw identity. It rejects a changed JSON basis,
added schema label or non-JSON media before retrieval. Other closure records keep
their existing exact JSON/JCS role rules; no wire discriminator is added.

The native projection reads that complete retained Common report before later
inventory/audit joins. Manifest, Common policy, mode, original evaluation time and
complete ordered claim scope must match the earlier request and raw result.
Domain verdict remains Common's original `not_evaluated`. A raw record claiming
current eligibility cannot promote refused Common/current fields. These are
necessary declaration/binding checks; actual Common execution, trusted source,
physical Clock, scientific/current admission and whole verification remain
separate obligations.

sections.heading: Actual Common result to earlier evaluation request
sections.excerpt:
`construct_evaluation_request` takes the original pair/campaign index, complete
native and Common policies, registry, trust, run identity, source limits and
explicit output store. Its configuration contains all twenty-five non-generated
request properties. Those properties are validated through the original pinned
request schema before retrieval or Common execution, with no dummy references.
A caller cannot select the generated subject, manifest, policy, envelopes, Common
report, run identity or request discriminator. Requested pair/claim scope, Common
policy and mode must match the independently selected caller inputs. Original
root-control references resolve the exact ordered caller control bytes.

The function calls the actual pair or campaign Common stage with the original
retained trust configuration. A refusal preserves its original locating exception
and creates no report or request output. A returned result must match the actual
manifest, policy, registry, mode, time and complete claim scope. The serializer
retains all fifteen genuine Common fields and every ordered observation/reason,
including original nulls and reference omissions, without a new wire tag.

Only then are the seven generated request properties added to the unchanged
caller configuration. The complete raw report and all thirty-two request fields
pass their original grammars and shared acquisition limits before either is
stored under its actual original identity. No evaluator, signer, reseal or current
state mutation occurs here. Actual successful output, qualified profiles and the
complete owning verification context/operation retain their independent evidence
requirements.

sections.heading: Later evaluation input construction
sections.excerpt:
`construct_evaluation_inputs` consumes the independently retained whole request
and actual raw output plus all eight original later observation properties.
It admits their fixed properties through the unchanged forty-field schema before
source lookup, without dummy references or generated-field overrides. The request's
twenty-six carried fields and raw evaluated pair/claim IDs remain unchanged.
Schema, request/raw references and the original whole-binding rule are generated
from those actual sources; no native or wrapper identity enters the context.

The complete forty-field document receives its original grammar check. Whole
request/raw/scope, retained raw Common report, prior input inventory, original
projection recipe and linked completed parent records must agree before the
context is stored. The same acquisition budget retains all actual earlier bytes,
attempts, schema sources and missing controls. Original inputs are never rewritten.
No engine, Common rerun, signer, reseal or timestamp repair occurs.

Source, oracle and case-record observations use their original availability
wrappers. Their referenced values and availability must agree with the raw
observations; an unavailable later declaration cannot hide an available raw
reference. The raw coverage inventory also remains the request's original case
inventory. Matching declared identities grant no assurance or qualification.

This is a construction stage, not admitted evaluator or current evidence. Actual
successful completed evaluator/audit/context/native projection and full source,
role, temporal, physical Clock, security, scientific and current predicates remain
the owning verifier's separate obligations. The complete root verify operation and
its caller context still require integration and qualification.

sections.heading: Direct parent audit source reader
sections.excerpt:
`read_evaluation_process_audit` reads the original thirteen-field audit directly
from independently selected earlier request, raw output and evaluation Clock
references. It uses the fixed original request/raw schema resources for invocation
contracts, matches the selected evaluator source, environment and source inventory,
and checks full run, pair, claim and case scope. The same reader serves later-input
construction and native projection; it requires no future context or report digest.

It reads all seven linked parent records, joins their original invocation/start/end
identities and preserves terminal raw validation and reaping declarations. The
containment and cancellation configurations must match their observed selections,
resource limits, allowed input references and prior admission identities. Original
supervisor identities, five linked Clock events and each actual signal's run,
invocation, start and process-group identities must agree. All direct references
from the complete checked parent records, configurations, Clock and signal records
are acquired unchanged under the existing whole-operation budget. Opaque capture
bytes are retained without inventing further record types or traversal rules.

The reader returns the exact original audit bytes and writes no output. These are
source joins and full direct acquisitions; they establish no actual process run,
capture authenticity, temporal precedence, physical Clock, prior qualification,
containment, absence of cancellation or current authority. The owning runtime and
whole verifier still supply and establish those original predicates. Successful
completed parent/configuration/Clock/capture output remains unverified.

sections.heading: Whole native input production
sections.excerpt:
`construct_native_input` consumes the complete original pair or local batch
value, independent registry/source/store and all six bounds. It detaches and
rechecks every field through the existing input wire. A batch requires its entire
already retained raw request; any supplied pair request also has to match all
original fields. Original request whitespace and programme bytes remain unchanged.

The fixed native schema/source/traversal cohort is checked without replacing the
caller's qualification fields. Whole programme, format, compiler, target,
semantics, engine, resource, case and available order/source references are read
through the existing shared draft acquisition. Each complete eleven-field pair
input undergoes native grammar and genuine Common construction. Available and
unavailable branches and original assurance labels remain unchanged.

For a batch, all pairs prepare before output. The five-field native batch input
is bound to the unchanged prior request and the whole original ordered pair
inventory, then receives complete native/Common construction. Generated identities
and bytes remain in the same bounded acquisition until every member and batch
check succeeds. The final immutable writes must preserve their actual identities;
an earlier source/preparation refusal publishes no prepared pair. A storage
failure can leave completed immutable outputs, which remain original custody.

The return value contains the original native value and its actual retained input
reference. This is the witness pipeline's input stage; it executes no programme,
selects no signer and grants no profile, engine, source, scientific, physical Clock,
current or ready-certificate qualification. Root witness and its caller context
still require the full actual construction and qualificati

sections.heading: Original pair content production
sections.excerpt:
`construct_pair_certificate` consumes the retained complete native pair input and
all eight remaining metadata fields: identity, conversions, engines, oracles,
verdict, claims, ordered claim bindings and completeness. The metadata validator
uses only those original properties of the pinned thirteen-field schema and its
full original Common dependency, with no dummy source or generated-field override.
Original metadata and schema bytes stay in the same shared acquisition budget.

The independently selected pair policy is matched to its whole retained source.
Pair identity and full original policy/claim scope, complete ordered unique claim
bindings and the original case inventory must agree. The producer generates only
schema, pair identity/input and compiler/semantics references from the retained
original pair, then validates and constructs the entire original native content
through genuine Common. Immutable storage must retain that actual content identity.

The result is a content reference. This producer computes no verdict, executes no
programme and grants no ready tag, source/profile/scientific/physical Clock/current
qualification or signing authority. The owning witness runtime must supply actual
whole observations and establish readiness. Successful actual observed pair content
and its complete construction/qualification path remain unverified.

sections.heading: Controller parent process measurements
sections.excerpt:
The real controlled-engine entry point now retains the parent-visible process ID
and its actual monotonic start/end samples in `ControllerObservation`. The interval
starts at operation entry and ends after owned termination, reaping and custody
validation. `elapsed_nanoseconds` returns their exact difference without rounding.
The same final sample determines the unchanged outer timeout disposition.

These observations are retained on controller refusals as well as validated
transport. Pre-creation failures still produce no invented process identity or
returned interval. Monotonic samples provide no physical UTC Clock, independently
qualified duration, containment or native eligibility. The original parent-audit
producer still needs its full qualified sources and real run/Clock/capture bindings.

sections.heading: Immutable controller custody
sections.excerpt:
`execution.controller_storage.retain_controller_custody` reads the completed
controller directory before writing to an independent `OfflineObjectStore`.
No-follow descriptors admit regular files and directories under the caller's
entry, depth and byte bounds. Missing required originals, linked entries and
source/output overlap refuse before publication. The returned sorted inventory
preserves every file occurrence, while stored bytes retain genuine raw identities.
A separate raw JSON object records the actual captured PID, exit disposition and
monotonic interval. It is not a new native schema or physical Clock record.

The directory and destination are caller-controlled completed custody, without a
hostile concurrent writer. A storage failure can leave completed immutable objects.
The original controller tree is preserved. File acquisition conservatively applies
the remaining shared byte budget before reading each file, including repeated bytes.
The importer supplies custody for later producers; native raw-engine, run-receipt,
parent-audit and witness readiness still require their complete qualified bindings.

sections.heading: Execution and original-data joins
sections.excerpt:
The source library observes original circuit programmes and compiler output.
The entry points described here are source APIs. Complete certificate
operations and their common evidence and consumer integration remain under
development.

sections.heading: Controlled engine path
sections.excerpt:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Original["Original source, compiled bytes and declarations"] --> Adapter["Owned QCEC or PyZX observation adapter"]
    Adapter --> Controller["Controller request and separate process"]
    Controller --> Worker["Fixed owned QASM or QPY worker"]
    Worker --> Supplier["Genuine MQT QCEC or PyZX call"]
    Supplier --> Capture["Raw result, configuration and streams"]
    Capture --> Custody["Complete exported-custody validation"]
    Custody --> Observation["Typed observation and available artifact paths"]
```

The four controlled adapters select QCEC or PyZX and QASM or QPY explicitly.
They pass original source and compiled bytes, complete named dependencies,
requested supplier options, `ControllerPolicy` and `EngineLimits` into the
supervised capture. Received artifacts never choose an executable. Fixed
`WorkerKind` values select owned modules.

The controller retains its original envelope and inputs, starts a separate
process, captures bounded raw stdout and stderr, reaps that process and imports
its regular-file export. Custody validation joins the exported request,
programmes, ordered dependencies, applied configuration and actual result to
those originals. Unused and equal-byte dependency occurrences remain part of
the declaration. A digest match by itself cannot replace that join.

`SupervisedCapture` exposes executed, error or timeout state, the decoded
native outcome, actual elapsed time and existing artifact paths. A missing
result remains absent. QCEC criteria keep their original vocabulary; an
unsuccessful PyZX reduction does not become a definite difference. An
observation is separate from a current domain verification report.

sections.heading: Resource scopes
sections.excerpt:
| Configuration | Actual scope |
| --- | --- |
| Engine timeout | Owned engine preparation, exchange, validation, cleanup and custody interval |
| Engine qubits | Represented physical IR width, including declared ancillary wires |
| Engine operations | Static operation occurrences, including derived scalar gates and recursive containers |
| Engine input bytes | Original programme and declaration occurrences plus the encoded request |
| Engine output bytes | Aggregate retained native stdout and stderr |
| Engine memory | Per-engine virtual address-space cap |
| Startup memory | Separate soft cap before supplier imports |
| Controller policy | Separate controller address space, lifetime, request/export quotas and namespace storage |
| Worker storage | Separate finite inner namespace data capacity |

The six engine thresholds stay distinct from startup and controller controls.
Actual limits and observed runtime state are retained in receipts. BLAS and
OpenMP thread counts are fixed to one in the controller and worker environments;
QCEC's requested native execution options remain separate captured settings.
Caller-side preparation and validation retain elapsed checks, but hard
whole-caller memory and lifetime containment are not qualified.

sections.heading: Declared original inputs
sections.excerpt:
`ProgrammeInput` retains original reference, declared format, format-profile
reference, canonical logical qubit count and the two independent order
availabilities. `AvailableReference` retains value, source and assurance;

`PairInput` keeps the current pair-input declaration, including both programme

batch declaration is separate from a native batch-input evidence payload.
Repeated pair IDs refuse; identifiers remain exact UTF-8 scalar text with no
Unicode normalisation. The six format declarations do not expand the existing
engine converters' supported domains.

`resolve_programme` takes the full genuine original reference and an explicit
positive read cap from common limits. It retrieves original bytes, calls the
public common `reference_bytes` with the original selected metadata and complete
limits, and requires full reference equality. It does not rewrite a programme or
infer a profile, source-width agreement, ordering, ancilla semantics or
equivalence. The genuine public `Limits.validate` method checks all six fields
before retrieval. The byte helper independently checks those complete limits
when constructing the actual reference.
The `input_wire` source API decodes and encodes the complete current pair and
local ordered batch mappings. Nested references use the genu

sections.heading: Compiler and metadata path
sections.excerpt:
`execute_compiler` retains the original QPY and selects one fixed owned compiler
case. Its worker emits prior public compiler arguments, ordered callbacks,
source observations and complete output bytes. The caller retains raw frames
and stderr and reaps the worker. This compiler path has its own legacy
containment; it does not acquire the engine controller's complete admission
contract by using the same namespace helpers.

Compiler frame validation checks source, arguments, ordered passes and output
custody. It independently loads the same input and output QPY through the SDK.
Exactly one circuit on each side is required; observed phase, original and
output widths, all five layout maps and availability must agree.

| Map | Observed interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Full initial | Original virtual wire position to initial physical position, including added wires |
| Full final | Original virtual wire position to final physical position, including added wires |
| Routing | Permutation of the emitted physical wire positions |
| Logical initial | Initial physical positions of original source wires |
| Logical final | Final physical positions of original source wires |

Missing layout remains explicit absence. Full physical maps are checked as
bijections, logical maps as injections, and their routing and ordering must
agree. A mutually consistent shortened record cannot replace the original
complete input/output association.

Byte replay compares retained original outputs exactly. Repeated SDK QPY dumps
can differ in layout-register serialisation even when circuit and map
observations are unchanged. Those byte differences remain visible; source
immutability is checked against retained SDK circuit state and layout
observations rather than assumed repeat serialisation.

sections.heading: Original draft declarations
sections.excerpt:
`WitnessDraft` keeps pair ID, original pair input, certificate and construction
policy references. `ReadyDraftMember` binds that complete nested declaration to
the exact outer pair identity. `RefusedDraftMember` and
`NotEvaluatedDraftMember` retain different original outcomes, each with its raw
diagnostic and complete ordered custody. They do not invent a ready draft or
certificate.

`BatchWitnessDraft` keeps the complete nonempty ordered member tuple, original
local request and campaign policy references, and the explicit
`transpile_witness.batch_input.v2` native input binding. Duplicate pair IDs or
another branch refuse. `draft_wire` encodes and decodes the complete original
local_io.v2 pair/campaign declarations and nested branches through genuine public
Common reference methods. A raw diagnostic requires raw bytes and an omitted
schema declaration. These source APIs check declarations and identity bindings;
they do not fetch or admit referenced certificates, policies or native inputs.

sections.heading: Original sealed output declarations
sections.excerpt:
`SealedWitness` retains the full pair input, certificate, common manifest and
ordered envelope references. `ReadySealedMember` requires exact outer/nested
pair identity. `RefusedSealedMember` and `NotEvaluatedSealedMember` retain the

index references with an omitted schema. The index is support rather than a

`sealed_wire` maps the entire closed local_io.v2 declarations and member
branches through genuine public Common reference methods. Received unknown,

The complete `seal` operation remains under development.

All declared member pair inputs carry the current native `pair_input.v2`
version, pair certificates carry `certificate.v2`, and sealed manifests carry
`evidence_manifest_toolkit.manifest.v1`. Native roles require the original
JSON media type and JCS digest basis. These distinct roles cannot be replaced
by one identical full reference. This checks declarations rather than admitting
the referenced contents. Empty envelope tuples explicitly declare unsigned
custody; signature requirements remain subject to the actual policy, with no
unsigned fallbac

sections.excerpt:
`WitnessInspection` and `BatchWitnessInspection` retain complete original

without executing, decoding, normalising or expanding the pointer. Mapping
these values calls genuine Common reference methods and refuses mixed fields.
The public inspection read path is described below. Full verification and
qualified evaluation time remain under development.

`OfflineObjectStore` retains original programme and JSON bytes in an existing
caller-owned directory. `put` calls the genuine common `reference_bytes

sections.heading: Original native campaign input assembly
sections.excerpt:

request reference and independently retained native pair references. It validates

unique full references. Supplied values are decoded before comparison, and the

Assembly and serialization each use one acquisition budget for the entire

matching within serialization uses the same retained original bytes. The
consumer independently rejects returned bytes beyond its remaining budget,
including when a resolver ignores the requested cap. These reads cover this
input population; they do not traverse or admit the complete native evidence
graph or its source, policy and profile dependencies.

sections.heading: Original native document shape checks
sections.excerpt:
`read_native_json` requires the selected JSON/JCS role and complete genuine
reference, reads actual immutable original bytes under the blob and total cap,
then returns those same bytes after `validate_native_json` checks the shape.
The real Draft 2020-12 validator uses the original native schema and the exact
21684-byte manifest-schema dependency through an explicit in-memory referencing
registry. Received fields do not select schema resources, code or a network
retriever. No original schema or payload is rewritten.

The original subject and both static schema sources share a three-object count
and actual total-byte budget. Every JSON parse uses genuine Common strict
checks, and native date-time formats delegate to genuine `Utc`. The static

Common registry snapshot. This stage does not traverse declared data references
or check their semantic roles, policy bindings, domain/source qualification,

sections.heading: Complete explicit registry snapshot construction
sections.excerpt:
`construct_registry_snapshot(entries, revision=..., store=..., limits=...)`
uses the complete caller-selected population without adding entries implicitly.
All fourteen fields, original order, raw schema bytes, selectors, dependencies
and qualification declarations remain unchanged. A shared internal encoder also
serves the existing caller registry transport, avoiding a placeholder snapshot
reference during new construction.

The supplied canonical decimal revision is a source declaration. The whole
snapshot receives its own actual JSON/JCS reference, independent of any earlier
cohort. Static sources are retained unchanged in the actual offline store; all
further dependencies must be available through that resolver. Source count and
total bytes are checked before encoding, ordinary JSON output is bounded, and
genuine Common `seal` validates the entire registry and required closure. Only
its completed canonical snapshot is published. Earlier source objects may remain
after a refusal; no prior original is overwritten.

This is explicitly unsigned construction. It takes no old snapshot, control
envelopes, trust context, Clock or signer and grants no current or domain
acceptance. The actual source integration selects eight original Common and
twelve native entries, constructs the new twenty-entry snapshot with 235 original
selectors, and uses it to construct a genuine native batch input through Common.
Native support declarations stay `required_unqualified`. Installed/profile,
scientific, current-trust and the complete witness/seal operation gates remain open.

sections.excerpt:
`assemble_batch_draft` takes a complete native declaration, its actual stored

construction for that input. It rejects missing, reordered or substituted members
before source lookup. Original member wire records are copied through their full
codec before IO; final campaign identity comes from the matched original bytes.

Selected raw schemas and all acquired input, diagnostic, custody, policy and
certificate objects share one count and total-byte budget. Whole original
references and returned bytes are independently checked; duplicate custody
occurrences remain ordered while identical acquired objects charge once. Genuine
Common separately checks its complete closure depth and construction rules.
The acquisition identity is the digest, basis and declared byte length. Omission
of a schema name does not create another object or erase an earlier declaration;

Digest-only control retrieval preserves original bytes and checks their actual
canonical identity; it supplies no absent control role or authority.

Ready members require real stored native certificates with matching pair/input
identity, the selected original pair-policy binding and Common construction.
Negative members retain actual diagnostic and custody bytes. Their labels do not
prove engine/source qualification or eligibility. This stage joins construction
outcomes through raw JSON diagnostic records that retain their original pair ID
and complete pair-input reference. Both must match the original member. Raw work

sections.heading: Native batch construction and pre-manifest index
sections.excerpt:
`construct_batch_member_index` receives the complete original native input,
batch draft, actual sealed-member declarations and full native certificate bytes.
It detaches original transport values before IO and repeats actual request/pair
matching through draft assembly. Every member identity, branch, negative
diagnostic and ordered custody must remain unchanged. Native ready rows must
bind the original pair certificate, manifest and all envelope occurrences.
Negative native rows select raw complete sealed-member records, matched through

The whole native schema and genuine UTC parser validate the original certificate.
Claim IDs and bindings retain the prior required campaign claims and original
ordered pair scope, including every member for whole-campaign bindings. These
checks establish declaration bindings, not scientific content or current
eligibility. A native claim bound only to refused/unattempted pairs cannot carry

require. Full claim evaluation and complete campaign eligibility remain with
`seal`/`verify`.
Member-scoped bindings may retain a proper original subset, and partial custody
can retain every member; these declarations do not establish whole eligibility.
Native bytes, hidden member custody and actual selected schema/data
acquisitions share the finite original-source budget. The genuine public Common
constructor then checks the entire known native subject and required closure.
Only its completed canonical content is published into the original object store.

The returned `BatchMemberIndex` retains original input/policy/members plus the
actual native certificate

sections.heading: C0 manifest and final sealed campaign
sections.excerpt:
`serialise_batch_member_index` emits every original field through the existing
codec under bounded ordinary JSON output and genuine strict Common JSON checks.
`construct_sealed_batch` detaches the received index, retrieves its actual raw

source/condition/validation/measurement fields; Common never
discovers a local transport by executing it. Actual sources and whole subjects
share one acquisition budget.

Genuine Common seals the whole known manifest, including native payload claim

`SealResult.envelope_json` bytes. The final sealed value adds only its own manifest
and ordered envelope references to the unchanged original campaign. All signing
inputs must be present together before IO; a failure returns no sealed value and

scientific acceptance, current Clock/root authority or si

sections.heading: Complete original campaign verification declaration
sections.excerpt:
The local declaration refuses historical eligibility, eligibility with unavailable
members or refusal reasons, and reasons naming absent members. Repeated locating
reasons remain in their original order. Equal raw references are permitted: their
digest identity supplies no evaluation-role or independence admission. These
coherence checks do not evaluate the native report's thirteen gates.

`BatchWitnessVerification` retains the entire closed aggregate under local_io.v2
and the separate current `transpile_witness.batch_verification.v2` reference. Its
local index and unchanged Common report are raw support; the original manifest
and campaign-policy references retain their exact native roles. Member results
and locating reasons preserve the entire original order and unique member IDs.
Historical evaluation cannot declare current eligibility.

`evaluation_time` uses the genuine public Common `Utc` constructor. Original
Gregorian/leap/fraction syntax is checked by its owner; the token is not repaired
or converted to a floating-point time. The wire mapper retains its exact original
string. Use the genuine `Utc.compare` for instant ordering, since inherited string
ordering and equality preserve spelling. Parsing and comparing a token do not
qualify a Clock, its source or current capture. Those remain independent trusted
caller/context preconditions of the real verification operation.

The mapping API does not recompute acceptance, execute an engine, authenticate
Common receipts or admit native report contents. All 22 local families have
source definitions and mappings; their complete installed operation/profile
qualification remains under development.

sections.heading: Complete native registry configuration
sections.excerpt:
`native_registry_entries(limits=...)` loads the entire fixed twelve-entry native
cohort and 188 typed reference selectors through genuine public Common types.
Every original selector ID, step order, optional-absence rule, null refusal and
present-reference requirement is retained. Complete raw schema bodies are checked
against their independently selected original identities. Schema-resource metadata
uses `application/schema+json` and `raw_bytes`; native JSON payload identities use
their separately selected JSON/JCS basis.

All domain support remains `required_unqualified`, with absent verifier and
qualification references. The caller supplies its complete Common entry population
and separately pinned registry snapshot before real operations validate the whole
registry and closure. Source preparation grants no domain or trust admission.

`native_manifest_schema_bytes(limits=...)` retains the exact 21684-byte raw
manifest-schema dependency used by those native schemas. The caller places those
original bytes in its explicit resolver. Its raw identity differs from the Common
packaged manifest schema; the resources are preserved separately. No registry
snapshot, current trust, profile, signature or evidence verdict is manufactured.

sections.heading: Whole caller registry transport
sections.excerpt:
`parse_registry` and `decode_registry` retain the entire independently selected
local caller registry as genuine Common `SchemaRegistry`, `RegistryEntry`,
`ReferencePath` and `SchemaDependency` values. Each entry contains all fourteen
original fields, including the complete canonical Base64url schema bytes, nullable
domain references, role/support metadata and ordered selectors. Every raw schema
is matched against its full declared reference. Empty or repeated schema cohorts,
unselected fields, changed source bytes and payload metadata in a schema role

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.excerpt:
MITIGATION-WITNESS is a standalone Python library under development. It owns
measurement accounting and mitigation-witness domain interpretation. It calls
native supplier APIs rather than duplicating their quantum engines or common
evidence verification.

Current components preserve original inputs, apply explicit bounds, compute
statistical observations and retain unavailable qualifications. The top-level
installed API exposes CountInventory, CountLimits and RationalValue. Existing
plan, attach, evaluate, seal, inspect and render controllers load when explicitly
imported from the package. Measurement imports remain independent of their optional suppliers.
The custody attachment branch retains complete HAL/QPU originals, every source
row and every count/case binding through genuine supplier APIs. Byte and count
agreement does not qualify native attachment, origin, windows or prior evidence.
The evaluation source branch rechecks frozen circuit/count bindings, executes
every native source case and retains complete results or refusals. It raises
EvaluationUnavailable with its full attempt while native construction is absent.
Optional source construction preserves all seventeen known-answer and twenty-eight
estimate fields, actual run/environment byte references and missing execution
positions. Ideal inputs stay declared; no source candidate grants native admission.
Whole optional evaluation source replay preserves every fixed criterion, bound,
case and missing metric slot. Missing complete aggregate/estimate bindings keep
the whole candidate unavailable while all diagnostics remain.
Full plan, attach, evaluate, seal, verify, inspect and render acceptance and
command-line integration remain unfinished.

sections.heading: Component architecture
sections.excerpt:
MITIGATION-WITNESS owns domain interpretation and caller-facing observations.
Native suppliers retain ownership of quantum computations and common evidence
handling. The current source is composed of Python responsibilities; there is
no separately implemented language backend or deployed service.

sections.heading: Original input and representation
sections.excerpt:
Counts retain all raw labels, multiplicities, explicit mappings and independently
reported totals. Rational quantities retain both original numerator and
denominator. Raw JSON capture preserves original bytes and every decoded field,
rejecting duplicate names, invalid Unicode, nonfinite values and exceeded bounds.

The schema catalogue binds exact local schema bytes and their closed dependency
graph. The source loader takes explicit external byte-pinned files; controlled
schemas remain outside the package. A successful schema observation establishes
shape under those schemas.
Reference declarations and native bindings describe required fields and
selectors; they do not authenticate a reference, grant a role or establish
that the original source is current.
